verifications.claim: ABC officially canceled the 22nd season of The Bachelorette on March 19, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'On Thursday, March 19, a Disney Entertainment Television spokesperson issued a statement announcing the cancellation of the series' 22nd season'; R2: 'An upcoming season of “The Bachelorette” was pulled on Thursday, ... March 19, 2026'; R5: 'ABC decided to scrap season 22 of “The Bachelorette” ... on Thursday, March 19.'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm ABC/Disney announced cancellation of season 22 on March 19, 2026.

verifications.claim: The 22nd season of The Bachelorette starred Taylor Frankie Paul.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'canceling Taylor Frankie Paul's season of The Bachelorette'; R2: 'Taylor Frankie Paul, who was set to star'; R3: 'canceling Taylor Frankie Paul’s season'; R4: 'Taylor Frankie Paul, who was set to lead'; R5: 'season 22 Bachelorette Taylor Frankie Paul'
verifications.reasoning: All sources explicitly state Taylor Frankie Paul was the star/lead of season 22.

verifications.claim: The cancellation followed the release of a 2023 video.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'after a 2023 video showed Paul throwing chairs'; R2: 'after a video of its star attacking ... from 2023'; R3: 'TMZ published leaked footage of a physical altercation from 2023'; R5: 'hours after TMZ published shocking footage ... recorded in 2023'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly link cancellation announcement to the same-day release of the 2023 video.

verifications.claim: The 2023 video showed Taylor Frankie Paul throwing chairs at her ex-boyfriend.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'a 2023 video showed Paul throwing chairs at her ex-boyfriend'; R2: 'throwing metal chairs at him'; R3: 'throwing metal barstools at him'; R5: 'throwing metal stools at her then-boyfriend'
verifications.reasoning: Sources precisely describe the 2023 video showing Paul throwing chairs/stools/barstools at her ex.

Dakota Mortensen'; R5: 'Paul ... throwing metal stools at her then-boyfriend Dakota Mortensen'

verifications.claim: Dakota Mortensen is Taylor Frankie Paul's ex-boyfriend.
verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.claim: Disney Entertainment Television stated, 'In light of the newly released video just surfaced today, we have made the decision to not move forward with the new season... at this time.'
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '“In light of the newly released video just surfaced today, we have made the decision to not move forward with the new season of The Bachelorette at this time, and our focus is on supporting the family,' the spokesperson said'; R2, R3, R5: similar exact phrasing
verifications.reasoning: Quote matches verbatim (with truncation) from Disney Entertainment Television spokesperson across sources.

verifications.claim: A rerun of American Idol was scheduled to fill the premiere time slot.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'A rerun of an “American Idol” episode will air on ABC at 8 p.m. ET on March 22 in place of “The Bachelorette” season 22 premiere.'
verifications.reasoning: R5 directly states a rerun of American Idol fills the slot.

verifications.claim: The Bachelorette season 22 was pulled from the schedule due to the New York Times investigation of the scandal
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: All: Cancellation due to 'newly released video' leaked by TMZ (e.g., R1: 'after a 2023 video showed Paul throwing chairs'); no mention of New York Times investigation as cause; R2/R4 are NYT articles reporting the video leak/cancellation.
verifications.reasoning: Sources unanimously attribute cancellation to TMZ-leaked video, not any NYT investigation; claim misattributes cause.
